name: Helena Revoredo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Helena Revoredo is chair of Prosegur, a Spanish private security company known for its fleet of 10,000 yellow armored trucks and 165,000 employees.
Her late husband, Herberto Gut, founded the company in 1976; Gut died in a car accident in 1997.
Her son, Christian, is Prosegur's CEO, and her daughter Chantal Gut sits on the board.
Prosegur, which went public in 1987, operates throughout Europe, Latin America and Asia.
Revoredo is involved in the Prosegur Foundation, which promotes education as well as inclusion for people with intellectual disabilities.
forbes_facts: Revoredo was the first woman to sit on the board of Endesa, Spain's largest electric utility company.
A patron of the arts, she serves as president of the International Council of Madrid's Royal Theatre.

name: Conni Jonsson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Conni Jonsson founded Swedish investment company EQT Partners AB in 1994.
He has been the chairman of the board since 2014.
Jonsson owns nearly 5% of EQT, which listed its shares on the Stockholm stock exchange in 2019.
EQT has roughly $62 billion (52 billion Euro) in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
forbes_facts: In 2020, Jonsson personally invested in elder care and housing companies after seeing his own mother's needs.

name: Wu Bo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Wu Bo chairs Estun Automation, a Chinese supplier of components for artificial intelligence equipment and industrial robots.
Nanjing Estun Automation went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015.
Wu Bo received his bachelor's degree and master's degree in mechanical engineering from Southeast Universtiy in Nanjing.

name: Kimbal Musk
forbes_bio: Kimbal Musk is the younger brother of the world's richest person, Elon Musk.
Kimbal is a billionaire thanks to his small stakes in Elon's giant companies, Tesla and SpaceX.
He has served as a director of Tesla since 2004. He owns 0.03% of the company and has netted more than $300 million (before taxes) exercising options and selling shares.
He previously served on the board of SpaceX and owns an estimated 0.05% of the $1.25 trillion company.

name: John Ruiz
forbes_bio: John H. Ruiz, a longtime Florida-based trial attorney, founded the Medicare and Medicaid litigation and technology firm MSP Recovery in 2014.
MSP, renamed Life Wallet in January 2023, identifies medical claims it believes another insurer, like auto or worker's compensation, should have paid and seeks to collect the difference.
Ruiz is CEO of LifeWallet and owns the majority of the $14.6 million (2021 revenue) company, which went public in a May 2022 SPAC deal with Lionheart Acquisition Corporation II.
In March 2023, LifeWallet announced it would not file its 2022 annual report within the prescribed period because management was "negotiating amendments to certain material agreements."
forbes_facts: Ruiz is an avid financial backer of some athletes at alma mater U Miami, including a two-year $800,000 deal for basketball player Nijel Pack, announced in 2022.
The son of Cuban immigrants, he was the first person in his family to attend college and law school.

name: Ma Bin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Ma Bin is the founder of Jiangsu Shemar Electric, a manufacturer of power equipment used in transmission substations and distribution systems. He stepped down as chairman in July 2025 and was succeeded by his daughter, Ma Cheng.
Ma, who founded the company in 1996, took it public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
In 2023, Shemar expanded into the U.S. and established its first subsidiary in Memphis, Tennessee.
Today the company's products are used in 100 countries and regions through manufacturers including Hitachi ABB, GE and Siemens.

name: Martin Herrenknecht
forbes_bio: Martin Herrenknecht founded tunnel construction machine-maker Herrenknecht AG, in 1977.
He owns almost 96% of the business, with the remaining shares held by his brother.
Herrenknecht had sales of 1.2 billion euros in 2023, its most recent financial disclosure.
Projects built using Herrenknecht machines include the Doha Metro in Qatar, the New York City  subway 7-line extension the 18-mile Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel in Virginia.

name: Lee Joon-ho
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2022); Hurun Global (2015-2016); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Lee Joon-ho is a cofounder of South Korea's largest internet portal, Naver.
He is the chairman of NHN, which was Naver's online-games business until the two split in 2013.
Lee sold $225 million worth of Naver shares in 2014 and another $115 million worth in 2016.
NHN's businesses now span from online gaming and digital payments to e-commerce and cloud services.
forbes_facts: He was an associate professor at Soongsil University,  a private Christian university in Seoul.
He is credited for developing the natural language search solution for Naver.

name: Shyam Sankar
sec_insider_companies: Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) - See Remarks; Ginkgo Bioworks Holdings, Inc. (DNA) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Palantir's chief technology officer, Sankar has worked with the company in various positions since 2006. When he joined the company, he was its 13th employee.
In June 2025, Sankar was one of four tech executives to join the U.S. Army Reserves' Executive Innovation Corps.
Sankar serves on the board of Gingko Bioworks, a biotech company working on genetically engineered bacteria.
He is also a trustee of the Hudson Institute, a right-leaning think tank based in Washington, D.C.
Sankar's wife, Pooja, worked as a software developer at Oracle, Kosmix and Facebook, before starting Piazza, a classroom discussion software.
